questions.prompt: Which hook is the earliest safe place to read a @ViewChild reference?
questions.explanation: The view isn't created during ngOnInit, so @ViewChild is undefined until ngAfterViewInit runs.

questions.prompt: What condition must be true for ngOnChanges to fire on an input?

options.text: Any property of the bound object is mutated
The bound value's reference changes (a new object/array/primitive)

questions.explanation: ngOnChanges triggers only on a new reference; mutating an existing object in place does not trigger it.

questions.prompt: What is the modern, recommended way to clean up an RxJS subscription tied to a component?

options.text: Pipe through takeUntilDestroyed() (with DestroyRef when outside an injection context)
Use ngDoCheck to check if destroyed

questions.explanation: takeUntilDestroyed() from @angular/core/rxjs-interop auto-completes on destroy, removing the 'forgot to unsubscribe' leak.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid putting expensive logic in ngDoCheck or ngAfterViewChecked?

options.text: They only run once, so it's wasteful
They run on every change detection cycle, so heavy work can run many times per interaction

questions.explanation: 'Check' hooks fire on every change detection run; expensive work there degrades performance.

questions.prompt: Order these lifecycle hooks in the sequence Angular calls them (for a component with inputs).
questions.explanation: The constructor runs first, then ngOnChanges before ngOnInit, then ngAfterViewInit, and finally ngOnDestroy at teardown.

questions.prompt: Which injectable class (since v16) lets you register a cleanup callback without implementing ngOnDestroy?
questions.explanation: DestroyRef.onDestroy() registers teardown, and it's what takeUntilDestroyed() uses under the hood.
